summary: SL-001 built the PS-028 whole-drive coverage panel and the five merged fixes (SC-015 mapped-drive remote check, SC-021 one source for the container-store wording, SC-044 singular counts, SC-046 reason-keyed wording, SC-047 tab/contract comments). The $MFT valid data length is the one measured part, the remainder is labelled 'space this account cannot read', and the report gains additive schema-1 fields. Suite went from 1111 to 1204 passing (30 files changed: 7 Core, 8 App, 14 test files, .taad/fitness.yaml). It was proved on SUBST rigs, this PC's real container store and the real Z:\ redirector. It was never run on the real whole C:\, which was the risk the spike asked about.

payload.reason: Slice built, reviewed and validated on everything reachable without a whole-drive scan; the real C:\ proof and the mapped-Z:\ window scan are person-run (SC-057, SC-058).
payload.summary: SL-001 built the PS-028 whole-drive coverage panel and the five merged fixes (SC-015 mapped-drive remote check, SC-021 one source for the container-store wording, SC-044 singular counts, SC-046 reason-keyed wording, SC-047 tab/contract comments). The $MFT valid data length is the one measured part, the remainder is labelled 'space this account cannot read', and the report gains additive schema-1 fields. Suite went from 1111 to 1204 passing (30 files changed: 7 Core, 8 App, 14 test files, .taad/fitness.yaml). It was proved on SUBST rigs, this PC's real container store and the real Z:\ redirector. It was never run on the real whole C:\, which was the risk the spike asked about.
payload.estimate_error: The tier was right and the effort was under-sized. Medium held: nothing broke, and the design's own retier to medium was justified by public API, report schema and native calls. But a panel plus five merged fixes came to 30 files (7 Core, 8 App, 14 test files, 1 fitness.yaml), +93 tests (1111 to 1204), three fitness rules, a corpus script, a name-clash checker and a new window script. Four gate stages ran twice (build-check, risk-spike, critique, code-review). The risk tier also understated what stayed unknown. The spike's whole-C:\ experiment (clauses a, b, c) never ran, so the slice's main-target claim shipped unmeasured behind SUBST-rig proof.

learned.lesson: The panel's behaviour on the real whole C:\ is unmeasured. Whether coverage.unseen >= the $MFT (10,540,285,952 B per U-001) and how many unreadable folders the panel lists were never observed. Every proof ran on SUBST rigs, this PC's real container store and Z:\. Treat the C:\ shape as unknown in the next slice that touches coverage, and do not cite 'validated' for it.
learned.evidence: Spike c-drive-ending-can-carry-panel stopped with no verdict ('needs you: allow one non-elevated report-mode scan of C:\'). Validate lists 'The panel on the real whole C:\' under not reached. SC-057 is the by-hand check.

learned.lesson: This repo already holds whole-C:\ scan records that answer count questions about this PC. Grep docs/design/*-runs and the seams docs before writing a spike that asks 'how many unreadable folders on C:\'. The spike's 20-folder bound was already contradicted by 559, which cost a major critique finding and a redesigned folder list (shallowest first, cap 20, 'and N more').
learned.evidence: Critique M1 cited docs/design/SL-095-runs/spike-87-2026-10-04/L.json:3 and :26 (C:\, 559 unreadable, cancelled at 3,313,298 entries) and docs/design/SL-089-seams.md:26 (446 rows under ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER). The design had called clause (c) 'undecided'.

learned.lesson: At every finished ending LargestFilesTab is visible, which caps the OutcomeTexts ScrollViewer at 76 px. Any new text added to the outcome area therefore lands out of view. Report-mode IsVisible and actualHeight cannot show that. Use CoveragePanel.top (TranslatePoint inside OutcomeTextsContent, null unless visible) against OutcomeTexts.actualHeight plus the new OutcomeTexts.verticalOffset key.
learned.evidence: MainWindow.xaml.cs:734 and MainWindow.xaml:296-311 (critique M2). Case A of tests/window/SL-001-CoveragePanel.Tests.ps1 measured top 113 px against 76 px shown, offset 0. Validate says nobody has seen a picture of the ending; the engine's only screen is the drive picker.

learned.lesson: The fitness rule 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends' is an allow-list with no xUnit twin. Any new Core file that names ScanStore (here Core.Analysis/SizeNotRead.cs) must be added to the list with a justification, and only Fitness op=check will find it. The design reviewed its own new rules but never read this existing one against its new Core file.
learned.evidence: Build round fixed 'the one declared architecture rule the engine found broken'. SizeNotRead.cs was added beside LargestFiles.cs and KindBreakdown.cs in .taad/fitness.yaml. The suite had passed 1204/1204 before that edit.

learned.lesson: A new tests/window/*.Tests.ps1 must be listed as a non-launcher in tests/window/AppArgumentCorpus.json, or AppArgumentTests fails. Before a design cites planted finish-line scripts such as E001-*, check that they exist in the tree. None of the six did, so the builder wrote tests/window/SL-001-CoveragePanel.Tests.ps1 (cases A to H) instead.
learned.evidence: Build deviation: 'The six E001-* finish-line scripts the design names are not in the tree'. An earlier run failed AppArgumentTests until the script was added to AppArgumentCorpus.json.

learned.lesson: The hook's stop mode fires from the 250 ms progress tick, so a stopped-scan window case needs a tree that outlasts the first tick. 700 folders was INCONCLUSIVE and 24,000 folders held. Put the minimum tree size in the design's case.
learned.evidence: Build: 'H was INCONCLUSIVE on a 700-folder tree (the scan ended before the first 250 ms tick) and held after the tree was made 24,000 folders' (hook stop at 15 folders).

learned.lesson: On this PC, 'a DriveType.Network letter is present' does not mean 'reachable'. Z:\ is a persistent mapping to \\100.109.48.75\collab and keeps DriveType Network when the server is down. A default-suite test that opens it passes or fails with that host. Kernel32.IsRemoteRoot opens the root and can block on a dead server, so it belongs on the bounded volume thread only. SC-010 should use DriveInfo.DriveType for the picker and reuse IsRemoteRoot only off the UI thread. IsRemoteRoot answers remote on FileRemoteProtocolInfo OR a \\?\UNC\ final path (measured on real Z:\: both agree; C:\ answers false with error 87).
learned.evidence: Code review major on VolumeUsageTests.EveryMappedNetworkDriveOnThisPcIsRemoteAndGetsNoFigure (waived N-005). Build/validate: Z:\ final path \\?\UNC\100.109.48.75\collab; the test was seen passing only while the server was up.

learned.lesson: The triage accepted fix m5 and the build acted on it before the critic checked it ('not put to the critic'), and the critique-review gate was sized out for this medium, minimal-project slice. m5 prescribed a real-device test, and that fix was the one that went wrong (a default-suite test against this PC's Z:\). When a prescribed fix adds a test that touches this PC's real devices (Z:\, the container store, C:\), have the critic execute or reason about the server-down and missing-device case before the build.
learned.evidence: Decision record for m5: critic_on_this_fix 'not put to the critic -- a build had already acted on it'. Code review then filed M1 against the test the fix produced. Critique-review #1: 'does not get its review reviewed'.

learned.lesson: When merged SC rows ride on a panel slice, size by surfaces touched, not by rows merged. Here the surfaces were Core native calls (Kernel32 plus the FailCriticalErrors counting test), public API (ScanStore.VolumeUsedMft), report schema 1, three fitness rules with a corpus script, a name-clash checker and the hook. That gave 30 files and +93 tests, and four stages ran twice. Count a fitness.yaml edit as three or more runs (lesson #486 held again: the plural rule still drew a spelling finding).
learned.evidence: git diff 21632dc5f..e41bdf639 lists 30 files (7 Core, 8 App, 14 tests, fitness.yaml). Rework: build-check x2, risk-spike x2, critique x2, code-review x2.

learned.lesson: The code review read 19 of 30 changed files only through `git diff` hunks or Grep lines, and none whole. MainWindow.xaml.cs lines 1-589, 700-885 and 916-1070 and Scanner.cs 1-369 and 415-623 were never seen as files. It still found a major and an input-class gap, but by running probes and window cases, not by reading. For a diff this wide the review should be split by file group, or the engine's 'not read' list should be fed back as a required second pass.
learned.evidence: Code review #1 'not read (measured)' lines: MainWindow.xaml.cs, Scanner.cs, Kernel32.cs, WindowReport.cs, ScanStore.cs and 14 others partly-opened; MainWindowNameClashCorpus.json never-opened.

what_went_wrong: build-check ran twice. The first pass returned 'halted' because an unbuilt slice's survey carried 'partial' with C5 and C8 'present' (existing behaviour to keep). The second said 'built anyway', so a whole gate lap was spent on a verdict the slice's own state made inevitable.

risk-spike ran twice and left its only decisive experiment undecided. The whole-C:\ scan needed the person's OK and the person was away, so the slice proceeded on one go (compressed files) and a model's decision. Clauses (a) finished-arm line, (b) unseen >= $MFT and (c) <= 20 unreadable folders were never measured. The slice shipped with its main-target proof outstanding (SC-057), and clause (c)'s bound was already contradicted by 559 in the repo's own records.

critique halted with 7 findings and passed on the second run. Both majors were about the real C:\ and were derivable from the repo and XAML before design: an uncapped 559-folder list, and a panel that always starts out of view (113 px into a 76 px region). The design had called the first an undecided spike clause.

The code review's one major (an always-on default-suite test that depends on this PC's Z:\ server being up) was waived as N-005 for 'no reproduction'. The default gate `eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx` therefore still goes red whenever \\100.109.48.75 is down. The test came from triage fix m5, which was never put to the critic. Validate saw it passing only while the server was reachable.

The 'no count in the App is written with a fixed plural' tripwire shipped blind to '{n} files', '{n:n0} files' and '{n:N0} Files'. These are the plainest ways to rewrite the SC-044 defect it exists to stop. The widened pattern was measured at 0 tree hits, but the finding was waived as N-004 and nothing landed. This is the third time a fitness spelling rule drew a spelling finding (lessons #486 and #846).

The design leaned on six planted E001-* finish-line scripts that are not in the tree. The builder wrote tests/window/SL-001-CoveragePanel.Tests.ps1 instead, and AppArgumentTests failed until it was listed in tests/window/AppArgumentCorpus.json. The design also named the opt-in SMB-LOOPBACK fact AMappedLoopbackShareGetsNoFigure, which was never written. An always-on Z:\ probe replaced it, and the build declared it as replacing the waived O-020 fact, not this one.

The design contradicted itself on the remainder wording. The component says it 'never contains the word measured', but the contract regex (?<!not |never )\bmeasured\b allows 'not measured', and the shipped text ends ', and it is not measured.'. A stricter planted check would fail on it.

Case H (hook stop) was INCONCLUSIVE on its first 700-folder tree because the scan ended before the first 250 ms tick, and had to be rebuilt at 24,000 folders. Nobody had put the tick dependency into the design's case.

missed.what: Triage accepted m5 (add a fact that runs only when a DriveType.Network letter is present, asserting Kernel32.IsRemoteRoot true and the composed read null) and the build acted on it without the critic's check. Nobody asked what happens when Z:\ stays DriveType.Network while \\100.109.48.75\collab is down. IsRemoteRoot's failed open returns null, so Assert.True(remote) fails, or the open hangs to FigureWait (45 s) twice. The default gate then goes red for a reason outside the code.

The fixed-plural tripwire's must-fire rows covered only today's four ':N0}' + lower-case-noun lines. The critic never ran the pattern on the plain spellings '{n} files', '{n:n0} files' and '{n:N0} Files', which write '1 files' the same way, and the rule's 'because' did not list them as gaps.
missed.caught_by: code-review input pass (IN-m1), run in both .NET and Python re

missed.what: The design put SizeNotRead.OnDisk(ScanStore) in Core.Analysis without checking it against the existing .taad/fitness.yaml allow-list rule 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends', which has no xUnit twin. A new Core file naming ScanStore breaks that rule.
missed.caught_by: build (the engine's fitness check; the allow-list was edited to name SizeNotRead.cs)

missed.what: The design's 14 cases and four contracts name six tests/window/E001-*.Tests.ps1 scripts as the checks. None exist in the tree, and the critic did not verify that the named check files exist. The builder wrote its own script, and a rule requires it be listed in tests/window/AppArgumentCorpus.json.

The CoveragePanelText component says the remainder text 'never contains the word measured'. The same design's Build contract pins only (?i)(?<!not |never )\bmeasured\b, and the shipped text ends ', and it is not measured.'. The critic did not reconcile the two statements, so a stricter planted check and the contract disagree.

The stopped-scan case (hook stop mode on a SUBST whole-drive tree) did not say the tree must outlast the hook's first 250 ms progress tick. A 700-folder tree ended before it, so the case was INCONCLUSIVE until the tree was 24,000 folders.

unknowns: On the real whole C:\ scanned non-elevated, is coverage.unseen at least the $MFT valid data length (10,540,285,952 B measured by U-001)? How many unreadable folders does the panel then name (cap 20 on screen; the earlier record had 559)? If unseen < $MFT, the panel silently falls back to the whole remainder and the report cannot say why. Review m4 asked for a raw `mft` key and was overridden.

What does a person see at a finished whole-drive ending? The panel starts 113 px into a texts region showing 76 px, and no picture of the ending exists. Is 'a scroll away' acceptable, or should the panel move (a Coverage tab in OutcomeTabs, or a larger cap)?

Does a finished scan of the mapped Z:\ itself end with no coverage line and no panel? Only a finished SUBST over one Z:\ subfolder (15,548 files, 28 s) and Z:\ stopped at 15 folders were observed. DFS letters and non-NTFS volumes were not reachable on this PC and are covered by unit tests only.
Does the default suite stay green with the Z:\ server down? Reasoning says no (the test is waived as N-005), but it was never observed failing.

candidates.title: Make the default suite independent of the mapped Z:\ server (VolumeUsageTests.EveryMappedNetworkDriveOnThisPcIsRemoteAndGetsNoFigure)
candidates.why: The test is a plain [Fact] with no Network trait, at about tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/VolumeUsageTests.cs:585-600 when the code review read it; the tree has since moved. It opens the root of every DriveType.Network letter. This PC's Z:\ is a persistent mapping to \\100.109.48.75\collab, which keeps DriveType Network when the server is down. With the server down, IsRemoteRoot's open returns null and Assert.True(remote) fails, or the open blocks to FigureWait (45 s), paid twice. Validate saw it passing only while the server was up. It was waived as N-005 for 'no reproduction'. The gate every stage runs, `eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx`, can therefore go red with no code change. Fix either way: put it behind [Trait("Network","SMB-LOOPBACK")], which FsaDefaultTestFilter already excludes, as the design's AMappedLoopbackShareGetsNoFigure planned; or assert Assert.NotEqual(false, remote) plus a null figure and treat TimeoutException as 'could not tell'. The always-on part may only assert IsRemoteRoot(SystemRoot) is false.

candidates.title: Widen the 'no count in the App is written with a fixed plural' fitness rule to the plain spellings
candidates.why: The rule appended under '# settled by SL-001' in .taad/fitness.yaml has the pattern \{[^{}\r\n]*:N0\}\s*(?:files|folders|links)\b. It is quiet on '{n} files', '{n:n0} files' and '{n:N0} Files', and each of those writes '1 files', the SC-044 defect. The code review ran the three in both .NET and Python re. Its proposed pattern (?i)\{[^{}\r\n]*\}\s*(?:files|folders|links)\b was measured at 0 hits in the App tree and quiet on the corpus's quiet rows. Do it by swapping the pattern, adding three must-fire rows to tests/bugs/SL-001-WrittenOnceRules.Tests.ps1 and naming the remaining gaps in the rule's 'because'. Run Fitness op=check and the corpus script and re-check the quiet rows. Waived as N-004.

candidates.title: Decide where the coverage panel shows at a finished ending; today it is 113 px down a 76 px region
candidates.why: Case A of tests/window/SL-001-CoveragePanel.Tests.ps1 records CoveragePanel.top 113 px against OutcomeTexts showing 76 px, offset 0. LargestFilesTab is visible at every finished ending (MainWindow.xaml.cs:734), which applies the 76 px MaxHeight (MainWindow.xaml:301-302). So the panel is never in view without scrolling, and validate says no picture of it exists. The sibling placement was the design's accepted taste decision against a 'Coverage' tab in OutcomeTabs. SC-057's by-hand C:\ run is the first time a person can see it. Rank this after that run: if a scroll away is not enough, either the tab or a taller cap needs a design pass that keeps Test-V001's four OutcomeDetail lines.

lessons_judged.why: The build-check re-read every cited line of the five merged briefs against the tree (all matched). The build also checked the three engine-appended fitness entries against the design word for word and kept them rather than finding duplicates.

The survey re-grepped each merged brief's symbols and line numbers (FolderTreeNode.cs:110, UnreadableRows.cs:107-110, MainWindow.xaml.cs:342-343/640/642, StartupHook.cs:763-771) and found none stale. It changed the opening step, though it turned up no staleness here.

The remote decision enumerated alias classes (mapped letter, DFS, SUBST over UNC, SUBST over a local folder, \\?\X:\, UNC root, junction). Code review then probed SUBST over Z:\ and over D:\ and a lower-case c:\ and found no defect.

The design retiered to medium on its 14-row case matrix and public API/schema changes. The matrix did drive the work (30 files, +93 tests). The slice was still larger in effort than the tier suggests.

The design read the hook's private FoldersIn, the Kernel32 path-call counting test (FailCriticalErrorsTests) and the rules-parity placement, and so moved FoldersIn into a linked file and put the SL-001 rules outside rules-parity. It still missed AppArgumentCorpus.json, the hook stop mode's 250 ms tick, and the absence of the E001 scripts.

The three rules were worded as tripwires with their gaps stated in 'because'. A corpus script ran at build, code review and validate. Even so the plural rule drew IN-m1, which confirms the lesson's prediction that a fitness edit draws spelling-class findings.

The design carried must-fire and must-stay-quiet rows (36 rows, corpus script, run over the real tree). The critic still did not run the plural pattern on plain spellings, and that rule remained a spelling list rather than a closed form, so IN-m1 came from code review.
Patterns use only (?i) at the start, character classes and lookahead. Build and code review compared .NET and Python re hit counts on all 36 rows and read the three entries through PyYAML.

The engine's fitness check caught the broken ScanStore allow-list at build, and code review ran Fitness op=check (105 rules hold) before filing. Both confirm that dotnet test alone does not carry these rules.

The design stated 'always, not sometimes' that every Stopped ending reaches AddVolumeInUse with Finished=false, so Build's finished guard decides it. Case H on a real stopped scan then confirmed no panel and the unchanged partial line.

Everything was observed through additive report fields (coverage, window CoveragePanel, OutcomeTexts verticalOffset), so validate could read the shipped exe's window in report mode. What a person sees is still unobserved: no picture exists.

filed.title: Check by hand: Allow one non-elevated, report-mode scan of the whole C:\ drive with this build. Read 'coverage' from the report: the panel is present; the unseen space against the $MFT (the spike's clause b); and how many unreadable folders the panel names (clause c).

Check by hand: Run the network pass this slice makes stale: N-001..N-004 and StalledShareTests. Add the new opt-in SMB-LOOPBACK fact (VolumeUsageTests.AMappedLoopbackShareGetsNoFigure, trait Network=SMB-LOOPBACK, already in FsaDefaultTestFilter) showing that a mapped loopback share gets VolumeUsed null, and confirm in the window that a scan of the mapped Z:\ shows no coverage line and no panel.
